chapter: Left out of the jazz books; Tatum, Handy and family
title: Elbert Topps, drummer Bibbs, and his mother guarding him from the chorus girls
summary: Topps was a fine trumpeter from Jackson, Mississippi, and Collins's mother protected him from the showgirls until the job closed.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: It doesn't have anything to do with his middle name, does it?
No, nothing, nothing, nothing at all. He was from Jackson, Mississippi. He went back to Jackson, Mississippi, I heard he died not too long ago. But he was a very nice --

He played trumpet. Very good trumpet player. And this guy -- the drummer's name was Bibbs, I can't think of his first name but his last name was Bibbs. I'm trying to think who was in this band. And they chorus girls here, and my mother would protect me because they were all hitting on me. And you know, she would --
Then she did, yes, then she did. Oh, they couldn't get within 10 feet of me. And you know, I --
Is that why you left Albert Topps' band?
